episodes.167215: An isolated thunderstorm produced some minor wind damage and large hail across far western Maryland during the evening hours.
episodes.167228: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed during the early to mid afternoon hours in northwest Alabama, spreading east through the early evening.  A few reports of large hail and damaging winds were received.
episodes.167248: Low-level southeasterly return flow set up across eastern New Mexico again on May 1, 2022. With the dryline developed north-to-south across the plains, this helped to set the stage for the development of afternoon thunderstorms. As the atmosphere destabilized, thunderstorms developed on the dryline before propagating northeast through the evening hours. While these thunderstorms prompted several Severe Thunderstorm Warnings, the only report received was penny-sized hail near Ragland.
episodes.167279: A frontal boundary and associated mid-upper level shortwave forced a small area of scattered supercell-like convection across the Central Midlands. Deep dry air aloft and sufficient cloud layer shear produced an environment primarily conducive for hail, especially given the isolated storm mode. The scattered convection produced numerous hail reports including multiple significant hail reports up to 2.
episodes.167300: Moisture quickly returned to West Texas during the day on the first ahead of an approaching upper level short wave. In response, scattered thunderstorms rapidly developed late Sunday afternoon. Relatively strong wind shear and moderate instability spurred several of the storms to rotate and produce very large hail. The configuration of the increasing and turning winds with height were right to favor splitting supercell storms. The left splits raced north-northeastward bringing brief heavy rain, large hail, and sporadic wind gusts. Golf ball to baseball size hail fell from the strongest of these northward-racing storms. Western portions of Levelland experienced extensive damage, primarily from shattered glass. The right splits moved slowly to the east, producing locally heavy rains. These storms also dropped huge hail with one greater than baseball size near O'Donnell (Lynn County).
episodes.167306: A cold front passing through West Virginia on the afternoon of May 1st prompted a few showers and thunderstorms. One particular storm grew strong enough to produce half dollar sized hail in Clay County.
episodes.167750: A weak stationary boundary extended from portions of Deep East Texas into Central Louisiana during the afternoon of May 1st, with a weak upper trough lingering over the Lower Mississippi Valley. Warm, moist, and unstable air remained in place near and just north of the front over Central Louisiana, with the lingering trough focusing large scale ascent for scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. An isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Northeast Grant Parish, producing large hail near the Georgetown community before weakening during the early evening hours.
episodes.167834: An area of low pressure moved slowly across northern Kansas and south central Kansas during the late afternoon of May 2nd, 2022.  A warm front associated with the low pressure area, lifted north into southern Kansas, with supercell thunderstorms developing in the warm sector, as the warm front lifted north.  The supercells produced some one inch hail reports and an isolated damaging wind report.
episodes.168088: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a very brief microburst. The severe storm was located in the vicinity of a warm front extending northeast from a low over north Texas.
episodes.168115: A strong cold front pushed across the lower Virginia Piedmont Sunday afternoon and evening producing large hail and thunderstorm wind damage. Increased southerly flow and warm air advection helped push temperatures into upper 70s and low 80s with dewpoints in the 60s adding support for scattered shower and storm activity. Instabilities, mid -level lapse rates, and deep layer shear values were modest with MLCAPE (Mixed Layer Convective Available Potential Energy) near 1,000 j/kg, mid-level lapse rates of 6-8 degrees C per km, and 0-6 km bulk effect shear values around 40-50 kts.
episodes.168154: An upper air disturbance caused heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms.  Early on in the episode, a flash flood occurred over a portion of Maui along Piilani Highway.  Otherwise, the precipitation produced small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways, over other parts of Maui and on the Big Island.  No serious injuries were reported.
episodes.168637: A cold front moved through the Mid-South on May 1, 2022, and stalled over central Mississippi. It then moved back north, into the Mid-South, as a warm front on May 2, 2022. Southerly flow, a warm and moist air mass, coupled with an upper-level disturbance moving over the region produced showers and thunderstorms. Damaging wind and large hail were the main hazards.
episodes.168638: A cold front moved through the Mid-South on May 1, 2022, and stalled over central Mississippi. It then moved back north, into the Mid-South, as a warm front on May 2, 2022. Southerly flow, a warm and moist air mass, coupled with an upper-level disturbance moving over the region produced showers and thunderstorms. Damaging wind and large hail were the main hazards.
episodes.168681: A strong upper level low pressure system moved across Nevada and Utah. Very moist air was across most of West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. High instability and wind shear were also present. An upper level disturbance had moved over the area which provided additional lift. During the afternoon and evening hours, numerous severe thunderstorms developed across Southeast New Mexico and the Trans Pecos and moved across the Stockton Plateau and the Permian Basin. These storms produced multiple tornadoes, very large hail, heavy rainfall leading to localized flooding, and damaging winds.
episodes.168850: Showers and thunderstorms, mainly in broken lines, accompanied a cold front across the region during the afternoon and evening hours of May 1st. Moderate shear and instability, as well as mid-level dry air,  led to the development of several instances of severe thunderstorms.  Only a single hail/wind report each were received in Pennsylvania, as most wind damage reports were noted south of the Mason-Dixon Line.
episodes.168851: Showers and thunderstorms, mainly in broken lines, accompanied a cold front across the region during the afternoon and evening hours of May 1st. Moderate shear and instability, as well as mid-level dry air,  led to the development of several instances of severe thunderstorms, with damaging wind gusts being the primary impact.
episodes.169413: Thunderstorms developed across northern Texas and eastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 2nd, as a warm front approached the area from the south. The strongest storm produced damaging wind gusts in Choctaw County.||Thunderstorms redeveloped across portions of southeastern Oklahoma during the afternoon. Strong instability south of the warm front, combined with strong wind shear, supported an environment for supercell thunderstorms. One such storm produced a tornado and damaging wind in Le Flore County. ||Another round of severe thunderstorms, which developed along the dry line across central Oklahoma during the afternoon, moved through eastern Oklahoma during the evening in the form of a squall line. The strongest storms within this line produced damaging wind gusts and large hail up to quarter size. A brief tornado also occurred in Cherokee County.
episodes.169414: Thunderstorms developed across portions of southeastern Oklahoma and west central Arkansas during the afternoon of the 2nd. Strong instability south of a warm front, combined with strong wind shear, supported an environment for supercell thunderstorms. One such storm moved across Sebastian County, producing hail up to golf ball size and damaging wind gusts. ||Another round of severe thunderstorms that developed along the dry line across central Oklahoma during the afternoon moved through northwestern Arkansas during the evening in the form of a squall line. The strongest storms within this line produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169501: Severe thunderstorms developed across the eastern plains late in the day and into the evening time frame. These storms were isolated and remained in Bent and Prowers Counties, with large hail and wind gusts up to around 65 MPH occurring with the strongest storms.
episodes.169614: A northward moving warm front and an eastward-mixing dryline both contributed to the development of showers and thunderstorms the evening of Sunday May 1. The highest thunderstorm coverage was west of I-35 and associated with the dryline. A few warnings were issued but only one storm produced wind damage.
episodes.169643: An upper level shortwave trough moved across northern Mexico and generated thunderstorms over the mountains. One of these storms moved into Texas and produced large hail.
episodes.169664: A dryline was the main focus for storm development during the afternoon of the 2nd as a compact upper wave crossed the area. Numerous storms led to reports of hail, high winds, and a few tornadoes through the afternoon and evening.
episodes.169695: The combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles saw an influx of moisture from the Gulf of Mexico on May 1st. This axis of low level moisture followed the Rio Grande before moving north up over west Texas. This created an unstable environment primed for severe thunderstorms from the Midland/Odessa area up through the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles. Thunderstorms initiated along the New Mexico/Texas state line and moved east to northeast depending on the nature of the storm. Multiple supercells formed in the late afternoon into evening hours. These supercells had plenty of moisture, instability and increasing winds with height that enabled them to become severe with very large hail and damaging winds which exceeded 80 mph in some cases.
episodes.169696: The combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles saw an influx of moisture from the Gulf of Mexico on May 1st. This axis of low level moisture followed the Rio Grande before moving north up over west Texas. This created an unstable environment primed for severe thunderstorms from the Midland/Odessa area up through the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles. Thunderstorms initiated along the New Mexico/Texas state line and moved east to northeast depending on the nature of the storm. Multiple supercells formed in the late afternoon into evening hours. These supercells had plenty of moisture, instability and increasing winds with height that enabled them to become severe with very large hail and damaging winds which exceeded 80 mph in some cases.
episodes.169793: A few rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms developed through May 5th. The bulk of the active weather took place from late on May 4th into the 5th as a cold front moved into the state from the northwest. In addition to severe weather reports of damaging wind and hail, very heavy rain fell from northeast Oklahoma eastward into Arkansas and across southern Missouri. This widespread heavy rain led to rises on area rivers as well as some flash flooding.
episodes.170008: A dryline was located well west of our area during the morning of May 1st. Low level southerly flow transported gulf moisture north across west central Texas during the day along with increasing instability. The combination of these ingredients help thunderstorms develop during the evening across the Big Country and Heartland. A few storms became severe and produced golf ball to baseball size hail.
episodes.170030: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over central Georgia as a cold front pushed through a moderately unstable atmosphere during the afternoon and evening. An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a reports of thunderstorm wind damage in central Georgia.
episodes.170322: A shortwave trough moved across the CWA with a dryline along the Hwy 283 corridor. The majority of the prime ingredients were to the east into south central Kansas and north central Oklahoma in the enhanced risk area. With decent shear and instability in the cold core part of the surface low, a few landspout tornadoes were produced along with some reports of severe hail.
episodes.170365: A thunderstorm produced one wind gust over 60 MPH.
episodes.170394: Several thunderstorm wind gusts in excess of 60 mph were recorded on the afternoon of May 2nd.
episodes.170491: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected Middle Tennessee on May 2 and again on May 3. A few reports of hail and damaging winds were received.

A thunderstorm moved across Pecos County and produced wind damage one mile southeast of Fort Stockton. Damage to travel trailers was reported in Rooney Park and trees were uprooted. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado in Pecos County approximately seven miles to the east northeast of Fort Stockton and two miles north of I-10. This tornado only briefly touched down, lasting less than a minute, and no damage was reported. Given that no damage indicators were accessible, this tornado was rated an EF-Unknown with unknown peak wind speeds. The path width is also unknown.

A thunderstorm produced wind damage in Pecos County two miles east northeast of Fort Stockton. This damage was determined to be caused by rear-flank downdraft winds with estimated peak wind speeds of 90 mph. The damage included multiple destroyed billboards, two damaged metal buildings, and two 18-wheelers flipped along I-10. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado in Scurry County in and near the town of Hermleigh. The tornado touched down approximately one mile northwest of Hermleigh near the intersection of County Road 4111 and County Road 4116. The tornado snapped numerous power poles as it crossed over County Road 4111 and continued moving east northeast. As the tornado approached US Highway 84, it produced EF-2 level damage at a home and detached garage where most of the roofing material was ripped off and concrete anchorage failure occurred. Large vehicles, trailers, and other debris were scattered up to 100 yards west of this home. The tornado continued onward, crossing US Highway 84 where it impacted a trailer park. Numerous mobile homes were flipped or tossed towards the west southwest as the backside of the tornadic circulation passed over the RV park. The tornado continued moving northeast and eventually occluded on the north side of town. Peak wind speeds in the tornado were estimated to be approximately 115 mph. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Scurry County and produced wind damage. The areas of damage were northwest of Hermleigh, locations to the south of a tornado that impacted the northwest side of Hermleigh, and a rural area east of Dunn. This damage included snapped power poles, significant damage to trees and roofs, and an overturned manufactured home. Given the orientation of the damage, and re-analyzing the radar data, this damage was determined to be caused by rear-flank downdraft winds, with estimated peak wind speeds of 85-100 mph. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

This tornado developed east of Horsepen Creek and south of Poteau Mountain Road, where trees were uprooted. The tornado moved northeast across Poteau Mountain Road, snapping and uprooting numerous trees, and then it destroyed an outbuilding, damaged a home, destroyed an RV, and blew the roof from an uninhabited home. The tornado became about 8/10 of a mile wide as it approached Gassaway Loop and then crossed Highway 83. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted, and outbuildings were destroyed through this area. The tornado continued to produce tree damage and outbuilding damage as it crossed Gilmore and Midway Roads, and then dissipated north of Midway Road. Based on this damage, maximum estimated wind in the tornado was 105 to 110 mph.
